question.:question/problem:
Write the equation of this circle in the form $(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2}={r}^{2}.$

{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
The equation of a circle with radius $r$  centered at the point $(a,b)$ in rectangular coordinates in standard form is

$$
(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2}={r}^{2}.
$$

In our case, the circle is centered at $(0,6)$ and the radius of the circle is $r=6$, so

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2} & ={r}^{2} \\ (x-0)^{2}+(y-6)^{2} & ={6}^{2} \\ {x}^{2}+(y-6)^{2} & =36.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the equation of the circle in rectangular coordinates is 

$$
{x}^{2}+(y-6)^{2}=36.
$$
